new_findings.what: async scheduling is ALREADY ON in the baseline: config/vllm.py:1185-1233 sets scheduler_config.async_scheduling=True by default for a non-pooling, non-speculative UniX executor. --async-scheduling is therefore verdict=already_present and must not consume a bench slot; conversely the observed prefill/decode serialization is NOT a missing-async-scheduling problem, it is a token-budget problem.
new_findings.expected_impact: negative knowledge: closes the most obvious candidate and redirects the stall explanation to max_num_batched_tokens

new_findings.what: Base launch args never set --max-num-batched-tokens, and on this device (63.98 GiB, below the 70 GiB threshold at engine/arg_utils.py:2592) the OPENAI_API_SERVER default is 2048. Prefill runs at only 1600-1840 prompt tok/s while steady-state decode runs 716-729 gen tok/s, i.e. the prefill path is the inefficient half of the schedule and each 2048-token step leaves generation at 27-278 tok/s.
new_findings.expected_impact: prefill chunk budget is the single lever on the 29% of wall clock that buys zero output tokens

new_findings.what: AITER a8w8 GEMM autotuning is inert on this host: the shipped tuned table /opt/envs/wu1w/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aiter/configs/a8w8_tuned_gemm.csv contains 26 gfx942 + 553 gfx950 rows and ZERO gfx90a rows, so all 5747 runtime GEMM shape lookups fell back to a heuristic default solution ('not found tuned config, will use default config'). Every dominant projection (N=34816/16384/17408/14336/5120, K=5120/6144/17408) is untuned. This is a genuine, large, but NOT config-addressable gap: closing it needs a GPU tuning run that writes a new CSV to a writable path (AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8 override at aiter/jit/core.py:96), which is KernelForge work, not a server-flag bench.
new_findings.expected_impact: largest unexploited decode+prefill lever; deferred to kernel backend rather than proposed as a variant
new_findings.accuracy_risk: none (same math, tuned kernel launch config)

new_findings.what: ReplaySSM (--use-replayssm) is present in this 0.28.0 build and would directly attack the dominant per-step HBM write, but config/vllm.py:2564 hard-gates it on model_config.supports_replayssm, which is a Nemotron-H-only interface (only nemotron_h.py implements it). Verdict for Qwen3.5 GDN: not_applicable.
new_findings.expected_impact: negative knowledge: closes a tempting candidate

new_findings.what: --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding is CUDA-only (MambaConfig.__post_init__ raises unless current_platform.is_cuda()), and is also hard-coupled to --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16. On gfx90a it cannot be used, so an fp16 SSM cache cannot get the rounding-scheme mitigation if the accuracy gate rejects it; bf16 is the only viable narrowing and it needs no stochastic rounding.
new_findings.expected_impact: bounds the fallback options for the fp16 variant of the state-cache candidate

new_findings.what: Model geometry confirms the state cache dominates decode traffic: 64 layers with full_attention_interval=4 -> 48 GDN layers; linear_num_value_heads=48, linear_value_head_dim=128, linear_num_key_heads=16, linear_key_head_dim=128 -> recurrent state 48*128*128*4B = 3.15 MB per layer per request, ~151 MB per request across the 48 GDN layers at fp32. head_dim=256 for the 16 full-attention layers is what pins the attention block size to 784 tokens (server.log:42-43).
new_findings.expected_impact: sizes the payoff of the fp32->bf16 state-cache candidate (halves 3.15 MB read+write per layer per step x 48 layers x 64 reqs)

proposal_set.name: gdn-state-cache-bf16
kb_evidence: hint 3 (research_hints.md ##3): GDN recurrent state is fp32 only because the checkpoint declares mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and Qwen3_5ForConditionalGenerationConfig auto-adopts it, not because a kernel requires fp32; state cache is the largest per-step HBM traffic source at conc=64

verified: config/cache.py:38 MambaDType accepts 'bfloat16'; engine/arg_utils.py:1237 exposes --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype; model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py:385,597 passes cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype into MambaStateDtypeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_dtype; model_executor/models/config.py:781-805 user value overrides the checkpoint declaration (it only logs a warning)
proposal_set.reason: Halves the fp32 delta-rule recurrent state that every decode step reads and writes across all 48 GDN layers (~3.15 MB/layer/request, 64 requests in flight). At conc=64 with GPU KV usage peaking at 57% the decode step is state-traffic bound, not compute bound, so cutting the widest per-step HBM stream is the highest-confidence decode-speed lever available. Note the GDN kernels accumulate gating in fp32 internally (qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:2008-2015 casts inputs to tl.float32), so the change narrows the stored state rather than the recurrence math.

proposal_set.name: prefill-chunk-budget-4096
kb_evidence: hint 1: prefill and decode are almost fully serialized - 5 waves x (38.5s prefill + 94.5s decode) = 665s vs 639.3s measured; ~29% of wall clock buys zero output tokens, so prefill-side levers are worth as much as decode-speed levers

hint 2: capacity is NOT binding (KV usage peaks 57.3%, Waiting: 0), so trading a little KV memory for activation headroom is free - gpu-memory-utilization itself is a dead end and is deliberately not touched here
proposal_set.reason: The base args never set this flag, so on a 63.98 GiB device (under the 70 GiB branch at arg_utils.py:2592) the API-server default of 2048 applies. Prefill only reaches 1600-1840 prompt tok/s while decode reaches 716-729 gen tok/s, i.e. the 1024-token prompts are being chewed through in small, GEMM-inefficient steps and each such step collapses generation to 27-278 tok/s. Doubling the token budget roughly halves the number of prefill-dominated steps and raises M on every projection, which is exactly where the untuned AITER a8w8 kernels lose the most. Peak activation grows ~1.2 GiB -> ~2.4 GiB out of 34.8 GiB of KV headroom, well inside the non-binding capacity margin.

proposal_set.name: decoder-attn-triton-backend
kb_evidence: hint 4: the decoder attention backend was selected by elimination, not merit - ROCM_ATTN was used only because TURBOQUANT was rejected for AttentionType.DECODER, and ROCM_ATTN itself then logged a fallback to the Triton chunked_prefill_paged_decode kernel
distinct from the AITER fmha_v3 ASM path that platform law 11 rules out for head_dim=256
proposal_set.reason: Baseline log line 32 shows the selector overriding to ROCM_ATTN, then line 61 shows ROCM_ATTN immediately abandoning its own custom paged-attention kernel ('Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation') because head_dim=256 with the 784-token hybrid-aligned block size is outside the native LDS-supported layout. So the run is paying the ROCM_ATTN wrapper's legacy KV layout and non-standard-block-size routing to reach a Triton kernel that TRITON_ATTN would select directly and support natively (rocm_attn.py:193 documents exactly this detour for qwen3_5 at 784/1056). Same math, one fewer translation layer on the 16 full-attention layers.
source_evidence: runs/baseline/51ac28ff8aed4ad59746fdb889fae7bb/benchmark_vllm_20260915_103510/server.log:32 (rocm.py:703 TURBOQUANT rejected -> ROCM_ATTN), :61 (chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:463 fallback warning), :42 (attention block size forced to 784)

residual_questions: Does the accuracy gate floor allow a bf16 GDN recurrent state on this W8A8 checkpoint (baseline 0.9674)? gdn-state-cache-bf16 should be benched with a tightened floor; if it fails, --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 is the natural second try (it is the dtype the upstream stochastic-rounding path was designed for, though that mitigation is CUDA-only on gfx90a).

pr_monitor was disabled this round (ir3_auto) and INFERENCEX_PATH was unset, so no upstream vLLM/ROCm PR survey and no reference launch script was reachable. All three candidates are config-only against the installed 0.28.0+rocm723 tree. A round with pr_monitor enabled should specifically survey (a) GDN decode kernels for gfx90a and (b) whether upstream has relaxed --use-replayssm beyond Nemotron-H.

Should the Coordinator hand KernelForge the gfx90a AITER a8w8 tuned-GEMM gap? 5747 untuned shape lookups with a shipped table containing zero gfx90a rows is likely the single biggest remaining lever, and no server flag reaches it.

Is MTP worth benching at all on the sealed corpus? Framework support is confirmed present (qwen3_5_mtp.py registered, 15 usable mtp.* weights, n_predict auto-derived), but RANDOM_RANGE_RATIO=1 collapses draft acceptance, so any measured number is uninformative either way.
payload.summary: Surveyed the installed 0.28.0+rocm723 tree against the two live inefficiencies (29% of wall clock prefill-stalled; decode bound by fp32 GDN state traffic). Ruled out async scheduling (already default-on), KV/gpu-memory-utilization tuning (capacity non-binding), --use-replayssm (Nemotron-H-only gate), and mamba stochastic rounding (CUDA-only). Proposes 3 ranked config-only candidates: bf16 GDN ssm state cache, 4096-token prefill chunk budget (default is 2048 on this 64 GB device), and direct TRITON_ATTN to skip ROCM_ATTN's confirmed Triton fallback. AITER tuned-GEMM has zero gfx90a rows (5747 untuned lookups) - flagged for KernelForge, not proposed as a variant.
